Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border functionality exists at least partially through (a) WAEMU regional payment infrastructure (STAR-UEMOA RTGS supports participants including national public treasuries and banks across the union), and (b) international remittance reception into Wave wallets via partnerships (e.g., UBA Senegal/TerraPay/Wave enabling reception of international remittances to Wave e-wallets). ([BCEAO – STAR-UEMOA description](https://www.bceao.int/en/content/payment-systems-management);[TerraPay press release on Wave remittances to Senegal](https://www.terrapay.com/media/united-bank-of-africa-senegal-terrapay-and-wave-digital-finance-join-forces-to-enable-the-reception-of-international-remittance-transfers-enhance-financial-inclusion-in-senegal/))
revision_notes: Original score of 4 (Partially functional) confirmed. Both cited sources were fetched and read: the BCEAO payment systems page (general STAR-UEMOA/SICA-UEMOA description, still current) and the TerraPay press release (August 2023, confirms Wave's inbound international remittance reception). Fresher and more directly relevant evidence was found: the BCEAO officially launched the WAEMU-wide interoperable instant payment platform PI-SPI on 30 September 2025, covering Senegal and seven other WAEMU states, with a published pilot participant list (BCEAO communique, 31 July 2025) naming several Senegalese banks and e-money issuers already connected. This is a genuine instant payment system with built-in regional cross-border reach and supersedes STAR-UEMOA as the strongest evidentiary basis for the score. Onboarding of the wider payment sector is explicitly still in progress (BCEAO called on further institutions to join at launch), so 'Partially functional' remains the accurate code rather than 'Fully functional'; this is not a top-of-scale case. Senegal was not found among PAPSS's live participant countries (16 countries as of June 2025), so PAPSS does not currently support the score. Score confirmed unchanged at 4; year updated to 2025 to reflect the PI-SPI launch as the freshest authoritative evidence.
revised_comments: Senegal's instant payment cross-border functionality is partially in place. The BCEAO officially launched the Plateforme Interopérable du Système de Paiement Instantané (PI-SPI) on 30 September 2025, an interoperable instant payment platform accessible across all eight WAEMU member states, including Senegal. A number of Senegalese banks, microfinance institutions and e-money issuers are already connected as pilot participants, with onboarding of the wider payment sector ongoing. Senegal is also linked to the region's STAR-UEMOA real-time gross settlement system operated by the BCEAO. Separately, since 2023 Wave e-wallets in Senegal have been able to receive international remittances from corridors including France, Spain, Germany and the UAE, via a partnership between UBA Senegal, TerraPay and Wave. Senegal does not yet appear among the live participant countries of the continental Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS).
